result.topic_en: Riemann defines single-valued branches of log η(ω) and of the logarithms of k, k' and 2K/π as functions of ω via their behaviour as q → 0, using the η-function relations from Jacobi's Fundamenta nova, in order to derive their behaviour as ω approaches real rational values via first-order transformations.

Die Function $\log\eta(\omega)$ soll dadurch definirt werden, daß, wenn $y$ über alle Grenzen wächst, also $q = 1^{\frac{\omega}{2}}$ unendlich klein wird,
$\log\eta(\omega) - \frac{\omega\pi i}{12} = 0$
wird. Nun ist bekanntlich (Fundam. nova §36)
$\eta(2\omega)\,\eta(\frac{\omega}{2})\,\eta(\frac{1+\omega}{2}) = 1^{\frac{1}{48}}\eta(\omega)^3$
und
$\sqrt[4]{k} = 1^{\frac{1}{48}}\cdot\sqrt{2}\cdot\frac{\eta(2\omega)}{\eta(\frac{1+\omega}{2})}$
$\sqrt[4]{k'} = 1^{\frac{1}{48}}\cdot\frac{\eta(\frac{\omega}{2})}{\eta(\frac{1+\omega}{2})}$
$\sqrt{\frac{2K}{\pi}} = 1^{-\frac{1}{24}}\;\frac{\eta(\frac{1+\omega}{2})^2}{\eta(\omega)}$,
also zufolge der obigen Festsetzung
[-Ugl[?]-]

$= \frac{\pi i}{24} + 3\log\eta(\omega)$
